- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Green Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Vision and Context

The Green Party presents this manifesto against a backdrop of interlinked crises: cost of living pressures, climate emergency, and failing public services. Despite Britain's wealth, nurses rely on food banks, schools crumble, and healthcare is inaccessible. The party argues these crises share common solutions—climate action simultaneously delivers better services, warmer homes, and stronger communities. They position a Green vote as the only choice for genuine change and a secure future on a liveable planet.

## Health and Social Care

The NHS faces its worst crisis in 80 years—a deliberate consequence of Conservative underfunding and creeping privatisation. Greens commit to £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, £20bn capital investment, and restoring public health budgets. They would guarantee rapid GP access, NHS dentistry for all, and mental health treatment within 28 days. Crucially, they oppose all privatisation, backing the NHS Reinstatement Bill to keep healthcare public.

Social care would receive £20bn annually, introducing free personal care modelled on Scotland's system, alongside proper pay and career structures for carers.

## Housing

With over a million households on waiting lists and children in temporary accommodation, Greens propose 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. Their Fairer Greener Homes Guarantee includes £29bn for home insulation and £9bn for heat pumps over five years.

## Energy and Climate

The party demands urgent climate action, rejecting the 2050 net-zero target as insufficiently ambitious. They would ban new fossil fuel extraction, cancel licences like Rosebank, end fossil fuel subsidies, and introduce a carbon tax rising to £500 per tonne. Wind would provide 70% of electricity by 2030, with community ownership of energy infrastructure. Nuclear power would be phased out as expensive and dangerous.

## Economy and Work

Greens propose £40bn annually for green economic transformation, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. They would repeal anti-union legislation, introduce a £15 minimum wage, and cap pay ratios at 10:1. A wealth tax on assets above £10m and reformed capital gains tax would fund public services, raising £50-70bn annually.

## Welfare and Fairness

Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, the two-child cap abolished, disability benefits increased 5%, and carers' allowance raised 10%. The bedroom tax would be scrapped and benefit sanctions ended, moving toward Universal Basic Income.

## Environment and Nature

A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. Thirty percent of land and sea would be protected by 2030. Water companies would return to public ownership to end sewage pollution. Harmful pesticides including glyphosate would be banned, and a new Right to Roam introduced.

## Education

Greens would scrap tuition fees, restore maintenance grants, and work toward cancelling graduate debt. School funding would increase £8bn, OFSTED abolished, and high-stakes testing ended. Academies would return to local authority control, and private schools would lose charitable status.

## Transport

Public transport subsidies would reach £10bn annually, with railways publicly owned, free buses for under-18s, and £2.5bn yearly for cycling and walking infrastructure. Road building would end, domestic flights banned where trains take under three hours, and a frequent-flyer levy introduced.

## Democracy and Rights

Greens would replace first-past-the-post with proportional representation, give 16-year-olds the vote, abolish voter ID requirements, and replace the Lords with an elected chamber. They defend the Human Rights Act, support trans self-identification, and would scrap Prevent and recent anti-protest legislation.

## Migration

The hostile environment would end, safe asylum routes established, and detention ended except for public safety. Minimum income requirements for spousal visas would be removed, and asylum seekers permitted to work.

## Foreign Policy

Greens call for immediate permanent ceasefire in Gaza, Palestinian state recognition, and ending UK arms sales to Israel. They support rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty, and cancelling Trident. Overseas aid would rise to 1% of GNI.
